target.title: fix(scripts): retry Docker E2E after rejected resource caps
target.body:
Fixes #98601

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Docker E2E and package-backed Docker lanes can fail before the test container starts when the local Docker daemon accepts the command but rejects the default `--memory`, `--cpus`, or `--pids-limit` cgroup controls at container create/start time.

This can happen on nested, rootless, or otherwise constrained Docker hosts. Before this change, operators had to know to set `OPENCLAW_DOCKER_E2E_DISABLE_RESOURCE_LIMITS=1` manually; named-container and `--cidfile` runs could also remain blocked after a failed start attempt.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Docker run helpers now retry once without OpenClaw-injected default resource caps only when Docker reports a daemon/runtime cgroup or resource-limit create failure. The retry path preserves stderr, keeps ordinary Docker failures unchanged, caches the runtime resource-cap disable for later runs in the same process, and cleans failed `--name` / `--cidfile` container artifacts before retrying.

The package fallback helper receives the same behavior because it can run without the shared container helper in package-backed lanes. Explicit user-provided Docker run arguments remain on the retry; only OpenClaw's default injected caps are removed.

## User Impact

Developers and CI operators can run Docker E2E lanes on more host configurations without manually disabling resource limits. Normal hosts keep the existing capped Docker runs, and non-resource failures such as missing images still fail immediately without retrying as a different command.

## Evidence

Duplicate search before opening:

- `gh pr list -R openclaw/openclaw --state all --search "Docker cgroup resource limits pids limit fallback" --limit 20` returned only older unrelated sandbox/low-memory PRs (#41437, #39463).
- `gh issue list -R openclaw/openclaw --state all --search "Docker cgroup resource limits pids limit fallback" --limit 20` returned no issues.
- Searching the exact new warning text returned no existing issue or PR for this behavior.

Manual Bash proof for `scripts/lib/docker-e2e-container.sh` after this patch:

```text
--- docker-seen
run --memory 8g --cpus 16 --pids-limit 2048 --name gateway-test --cidfile /tmp/tmp.56caSlYtT5/gateway.cid demo
rm -f gateway-test
rm -f gateway-cid
run --name gateway-test --cidfile /tmp/tmp.56caSlYtT5/gateway.cid demo
run second
--- cidfile
removed
--- stderr
OCI runtime create failed: crun: controller pids is not available
Docker run resource limits were rejected by this daemon; retrying without default --memory/--cpus/--pids-limit flags.
```

Manual Bash proof for the package fallback path after this patch:

```text
--- docker-seen
run --memory 8g --cpus 8 --pids-limit 2048 --name package-gateway --cidfile /tmp/tmp.GV2mBfjcYw/package.cid demo
rm -f package-gateway
rm -f package-cid
run --name package-gateway --cidfile /tmp/tmp.GV2mBfjcYw/package.cid demo
run second
--- cidfile
removed
--- stderr
OCI runtime create failed: crun: cgroup controller pids is not available
Docker run resource limits were rejected by this daemon; retrying without default --memory/--cpus/--pids-limit flags.
```

Manual Bash proof that non-resource failures are not retried:

```text
status=42
--- docker-seen
run --memory 8g --cpus 16 --pids-limit 2048 missing
--- stderr
image not found
```

Local checks run:

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/check-docker-e2e-boundaries.mjs` passed.
- `F:\Codex\migrated\Administrator-Documents-Codex\2026-07-01\openclaw-pr-98358-proof\node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` passed.
- `F:\Codex\migrated\Administrator-Documents-Codex\2026-07-01\openclaw-pr-98358-proof\node_modules\.bin\oxlint.CMD test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts` passed.
- `$env:PYTHONUTF8='1'; python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` reported `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.

Focused Vitest note:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/docker-build-helper.test.ts --testNamePattern="retries Docker runs without default resource limits when cgroups reject them|returns non-resource Docker run failures without retrying|retries package-backed Docker runs without default resource limits when cgroups reject them"` reached the selected tests but this Windows checkout cannot spawn the Bash executable from Node. It failed at `execFileSync("bash", ["-lc", script])` with `spawnSync bash ENOENT`; a direct Node probe shows the same environment limitation even though PowerShell can launch the local `bash.cmd` shim. The manual Bash proofs above exercised the same helper behavior through that available shell path.
